final_narrative:
The differential metabolites are strongly enriched in **Eicosanoid Synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167, FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 1,251×), with five of the eight input compounds—arachidonic acid, 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A4—confirmed as pathway members.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the canonical upstream precursor. The KEGG reaction graph confirms it is connected bidirectionally to Leukotriene A4 (C00909) through an intermediate (C05356) in just two hops, indicating they are co-produced metabolites of the same oxidative cascade. Arachidonic acid is confirmed in multiple enriched pathways including Hemostasis and Fatty acid metabolism. Leukotriene A4 is confirmed in Arachidonic Acid Metabolism, Metabolism of lipids, and Fatty acid metabolism. Pathway membership for arachidonic acid and 5-HETE was independently confirmed against the SMPDB Arachidonic Acid Metabolism reference. 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-HETE (C04742) are confirmed members of the same eicosanoid synthesis cluster, branching from the same arachidonic acid pool.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of these five eicosanoids implicates intensified phospholipase-A₂-mediated arachidonic acid mobilization, followed by parallel downstream processing through the eicosanoid synthesis pathway. HETEs and leukotrienes are potent lipid mediators of inflammation, leukocyte chemotaxis, and vascular tone. Dopamine and fructose-1-phosphate fall outside the eicosanoid cluster and likely represent secondary metabolic consequences of the primary inflammatory-lipid shift.

In summary, the treatment group is characterized by a broad activation of the arachidonic acid–eicosanoid axis, with arachidonic acid and leukotriene A4 confirmed as interconnected nodes in tightly enriched lipid-signaling pathways including Arachidonic Acid Metabolism and Fatty acid metabolism.

**Limitations.** Several biological claims—including the glutathione compensation hypothesis for acetylcysteine and the COX/LOX enzymatic arm assignments for 15d-PGJ₂ and the HETEs—could not be verified against RaMP-DB pathway membership data and were therefore omitted or retracted. Fold-enrichment values for pathways ranked outside the top acceptance set are also not claimed. Additional targeted studies would be needed to confirm enzyme-level branch assignments and secondary metabolic effects.
